result.markdown: --- title: "W11 Lab: Specifying LVPA models in lavaan" date: today description: 'Download .qmd' format: html code-fold: true code-summary: "Show code" --- ## Purpose - Practice writing `lavaan()` model syntax for LVPA models (measurement model **plus** structural paths) Each scenario below gives you a research question and some background. In this rlab, for each scenario: 1. Decide which latent variables there are, and which indicators measure each one. 2. Decide which latent variables are **exogenous** and which are **endogenous**, and which way the structural paths go. 3. Write the model in lavaan syntax (just the model, we won't fit it in this class). - only change the Model, nothing else. 4. Run the `semPaths()` code to check that the diagram matches the model you intended. 5. Refer to lecture slides for relevant symbols. ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} These are **fictional scenarios**, and the data are placeholders. Because we never fit the models, the numbers do not matter, only the structure. ::: ## Setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} library(lavaan) library(semPlot) # Placeholder data: random numbers with the right column names. # lavaan() needs *some* data to build the model object; since we use # do.fit = FALSE, the values are never used. make_dat <- function(vars, n = 200) { as.data.frame(setNames(replicate(length(vars), rnorm(n), simplify = FALSE), vars)) } ``` ::: ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: --- # Scenario 1 **Research question.** Does a **growth mindset** predict students' **engagement in math**? **Background.** - A district surveyed 8th graders with four Likert items about how they think about ability and three items about their experience in math class (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree). - Researchers believe the four mindset items are driven by one construct, growth mindset, and the three engagement items by another, math engagement. - Growth mindset is expected to **affect** math engagement. Nothing in the model explains growth mindset. - Each item also has its own unique influences (wording, mood on the day, etc.). - **Scaling:** set the scale of each latent variable by fixing its **first loading to 1**. | Variable | Item | |----------|------| | `develop` | "My intelligence can be developed" | | `workhard` | "Working hard makes me smarter" | | `hardsubj` | "I can get better even at hard subjects" | | `mistakes` | "Mistakes help me learn" | | `enjoy` | "I enjoy math class" | | `focus` | "I stay focused during math" | | `persist` | "I keep trying when math gets hard" | ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # YOUR TURN vars1 <- c("develop", "workhard", "hardsubj", "mistakes", "enjoy", "focus", "persist") model1 <- " # ...your model here... " fit1 <- lavaan(model1, data = make_dat(vars1), do.fit = FALSE) semPaths(fit1, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel", layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0, sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4) ``` ::: ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} vars1 <- c("develop", "workhard", "hardsubj", "mistakes", "enjoy", "focus", "persist") model1 <- " mindset =~ 1*develop + workhard + hardsubj + mistakes engage =~ 1*enjoy + focus + persist engage ~ mindset mindset ~~ mindset engage ~~ engage develop ~~ develop workhard ~~ workhard hardsubj ~~ hardsubj mistakes ~~ mistakes enjoy ~~ enjoy focus ~~ focus persist ~~ persist " ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w11_rlab_lvpa_specification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=864} ::: ::: ::: ::: --- # Scenario 2 **Research question.** Does **second-language (L2) anxiety** lower **L2 proficiency**? **Background.** - Adult learners of English completed three anxiety scales and took a proficiency test with three sections (scores in points). - The anxiety scales are expected to reflect one construct, L2 anxiety. The three test sections are expected to reflect another, L2 proficiency. - Theory says anxiety **affects** proficiency. Nothing in the model explains anxiety. - **Scaling:** set the scale of **L2 anxiety** by fixing its **variance to 1** (so all of its loadings are free). Set the scale of **L2 proficiency** by fixing its **first loading to 1**. | Variable | Item | |----------|------| | `classroom` | classroom anxiety scale | | `speaking` | speaking anxiety scale | | `testanx` | test anxiety scale | | `listening` | listening section score | | `reading` | reading section score | | `writing` | writing section score | ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # YOUR TURN vars2 <- c("classroom", "speaking", "testanx", "listening", "reading", "writing") model2 <- " # ...your model here... " fit2 <- lavaan(model2, data = make_dat(vars2), do.fit = FALSE) semPaths(fit2, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel", layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0, sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4) ``` ::: ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} vars2 <- c("classroom", "speaking", "testanx", "listening", "reading", "writing") model2 <- " anx =~ NA*classroom + speaking + testanx prof =~ 1*listening + reading + writing prof ~ anx anx ~~ 1*anx prof ~~ prof classroom ~~ classroom speaking ~~ speaking testanx ~~ testanx listening ~~ listening reading ~~ reading writing ~~ writing " ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w11_rlab_lvpa_specification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=864} ::: ::: ::: ::: --- # Scenario 3 **Research question.** Does **academic motivation** predict students' **GPA**? **Background.** - High school students completed three motivation scales (scores in points). Their GPA was taken from school records. - The motivation scales are expected to reflect one construct, academic motivation. - GPA is a **single measured variable**, not a latent variable. It is **not** measured by multiple indicators. - Motivation is expected to **affect** GPA. Nothing in the model explains motivation. - Students' grade level was also collected but is not part of this research question. - **Scaling:** set the scale of motivation by fixing its **first loading to 1**. | Variable | Item | |----------|------| | `effort` | effort scale | | `homework` | homework completion scale | | `attend` | attendance scale | | `gpa` | grade point average | | `grade` | grade level (9-12) | ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # YOUR TURN vars3 <- c("effort", "homework", "attend", "gpa", "grade") model3 <- " # ...your model here... " fit3 <- lavaan(model3, data = make_dat(vars3), do.fit = FALSE) semPaths(fit3, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel", layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0, sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4) ``` ::: ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} vars3 <- c("effort", "homework", "attend", "gpa", "grade") model3 <- " # `grade` is not part of this research question, so it is left out motiv =~ 1*effort + homework + attend gpa ~ motiv motiv ~~ motiv gpa ~~ gpa effort ~~ effort homework ~~ homework attend ~~ attend " ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w11_rlab_lvpa_specification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: --- # Scenario 4 **Research question.** How do customers' **trust in a brand**, their **perceived product quality**, and their **purchase intention** affect one another? **Background.** - An online survey of shoppers asked a set of questions on 7-point agreement scales. - Theory says trust in the brand affects perceived quality, and perceived quality affects purchase intention. Trust is also expected to affect purchase intention **directly**, beyond its effect through quality. - Nothing in the model explains trust. - Two of the purchase-intention items were worded almost identically ("I plan to buy" and "I intend to buy"), so the researchers expect their unique parts (residuals) to **covary** beyond what purchase intention explains. - **Scaling:** set the scale of **trust** by fixing its **variance to 1** (so all of its loadings are free). Set the scale of the other two latent variables by fixing their **first loadings to 1**. | Variable | Item | |----------|------| | `reliable` | "The product is reliable" | | `buysoon` | "I will buy this product soon" | | `trustbrand` | "I trust this brand" | | `plantobuy` | "I plan to buy this product" | | `promises` | "This brand keeps its promises" | | `lasts` | "The product lasts a long time" | | `intendbuy` | "I intend to buy this product" | | `honest` | "This brand is honest with customers" | | `wellmade` | "The product is well made" | | `shopfreq` | "I shop online at least once a week" | ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # YOUR TURN vars4 <- c("reliable", "buysoon", "trustbrand", "plantobuy", "promises", "lasts", "intendbuy", "shopfreq", "honest", "wellmade") model4 <- " # ...your model here... " fit4 <- lavaan(model4, data = make_dat(vars4), do.fit = FALSE) semPaths(fit4, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel", layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0, sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4) ``` ::: ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} vars4 <- c("reliable", "buysoon", "trustbrand", "plantobuy", "promises", "lasts", "intendbuy", "shopfreq", "honest", "wellmade") model4 <- " # `shopfreq` measures none of the three constructs, so it is left out trust =~ NA*trustbrand + promises + honest qual =~ 1*wellmade + reliable + lasts intent =~ 1*buysoon + plantobuy + intendbuy qual ~ trust intent ~ qual + trust trust ~~ 1*trust qual ~~ qual intent ~~ intent trustbrand ~~ trustbrand promises ~~ promises honest ~~ honest wellmade ~~ wellmade reliable ~~ reliable lasts ~~ lasts buysoon ~~ buysoon plantobuy ~~ plantobuy intendbuy ~~ intendbuy plantobuy ~~ intendbuy " ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w11_rlab_lvpa_specification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ---
